subject: RE: Urgent: Hosted capacity spikes — next steps (Hosted -> Dedicated)
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@finservco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps on deployment mode

Hi Sarah — great to meet you and the FinServCo team today. Quick recap and agreed next steps from our discovery: 

- Primary goal: move fraud-detection scoring to an LLM-powered enrichment that must stay within strict latency SLOs (p95 < 120ms) and handle peak spikes during settlement windows.
- Current constraint: you're on our Hosted API today; call load test showed sustained bursts that pushed request queuing and caused token throttling during the 3am settlement run.
- Options discussed: continue on Hosted with strict rate-limits & caching (short-term), move to Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool, predictable throughput), or Private VPC for data isolation if procurement requires.

Immediate asks I captured:
1) FinServCo to confirm whether procurement requires a Private VPC contract or if Dedicated with network peering is acceptable (Sarah to confirm with procurement).
2) If Dedicated is acceptable, we'll provision a temporary dedicated pool for your June settlement window as an interim mitigation — needs signed SOW + capacity commit.
3) Laura to scope exact throughput and recommended VM/GPU profile (I asked her to run quick sizing based on the load test).

Attachments: load test summary attached (capacity_report.pdf).

I'll follow up internally to fast-track a provisioning plan once we hear from procurement. Thanks —
Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

1) Can Dedicated be provisioned within 48 hours if we approve?
2) What level of commitment do you need for a temporary provision vs. long-term contract?

Subject: Fwd: Urgent: Hosted capacity spikes — FinServCo needs provisioning fast

Team — forwarding. FinServCo has a hard timeline: next settlement run Tue 2026-06-16. They're leaning Dedicated (procurement) but need to know provisioning time and temporary/short-term commit options. Please see load test.

Laura — can you post a quick recommended config + ETA for spinning up a dedicated pool (2-4 GPUs)?
Marissa — I'll need help on commercial: what's the minimum short-term commit we can offer to cover a 2-week emergency window?
Rishi — please advise on operational support options and whether CS can stand up a runbook / on-call for the settlement window.

Connor

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: Hosted capacity spikes — FinServCo needs provisioning fast

Connor / all — quick sizing based on the attached capacity_report:
- Recommendation: Dedicated pool with 4x A10G-equivalent GPUs (mixed-quantized models) to hit p95 latency target under 2x observed peak.
- Provision ETA: 36-48 hours once approval and provisional billing are signed (we can spin up a temporary pool).
- Notes: If they need Private VPC + on-prem network provisioning, add ~10 business days for networking/KMS and procurement.

I can prepare an infra playbook for the settlement window; will need CS to validate failover fallback to smaller model variant.

Laura Bennett
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@finservco.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Hosted capacity spikes — next steps & commercial

Sarah — we can absolutely do a short-term emergency provisioning. Commercial options: 

1) Emergency short-term Dedicated (recommended): 2-week minimum at a day-rate premium (covers capacity reservation + priority support). We'll bill prorated and apply toward a longer Dedicated commit if you convert within 30 days.
2) Month-to-month Dedicated: 1-month minimum at standard Dedicated pricing (no premium).
3) Private VPC: needs longer procurement; not possible before Tue.

Connor — for this to go live for the Tue window we need: signed emergency SOW (I'll draft), PO or credit card provisional billing, and security contact for CS. I've attached a draft SOW (SOW_draft.docx) with emergency terms and a 2-week option.

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-06-15T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Hosted capacity spikes — operational plan for settlement window

Quick update from ops: we can staff an on-call run (covering June 16 window) and validate fallbacks (model variant + cache priming) if we get the dedicated pool provisioned by EOD Monday (2026-06-15). Action items: 

- Sarah / procurement: confirm acceptance of emergency SOW + provisional billing method (PO or CC) by EOD Mon (2026-06-15).
- Marissa: please send signed SOW (or electronic acceptance link) and PO details — Laura needs ticket to start infra provisioning.
- Laura: once PO/SOW receive, tag INF-2345 and provision 4x GPUs; post boot logs to the Jira link.
- Connor: coordinate handoff and share Slack channel (I created #finserv-dedicated).

If we miss EOD Monday, we can still mitigate with aggressive caching and rate shaping, but risk of queued requests during settlement increases.

Rishi Malhotra
Customer Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
